overview: Knut Eriksson was Swedish king from the Erik line who ruled after conflict with the Sverker dynasty. The profile is anchored by concrete turning points: 1167 — Rival king after killing Karl Sverkersson; 1173 — Recognized more widely.
He died in 1196, and his reign belongs to the wider story of Scandinavian state formation, Christianization, dynastic conflict, and northern Europe’s ties to England, the Baltic, and the Empire.

contentSections.title: Birth and early life
paragraphs: Knut Eriksson was born c. 1150. His family background is usually placed in House of Erik, though early Scandinavian genealogy can be uncertain and politically shaped.
Knut Eriksson's early life belonged to the medieval Scandinavian world, where kinship, sea routes, church contacts, assemblies, and armed followings shaped the opportunities available to a ruler.

contentSections.title: Character and Personality
paragraphs: Knut Eriksson, son of the sainted Eric IX, is remembered as a determined dynast who secured the Erik line's hold on the Swedish throne through the long feud with the Sverkers. The sources present a ruler who came to power by defeating and killing his rivals and who then held the crown for a substantial reign, consolidating royal authority and promoting the cult of his martyred father to bolster his legitimacy.

His reign is associated with the strengthening of the monarchy, the building of fortifications, and cooperation with the church and the powerful magnate Birger Brosa, suggesting a capable political operator. The use of his father's sanctity as a dynastic asset shows a shrewd grasp of the sources of royal legitimacy.

The personal man is faintly drawn, but the documented actions characterise the reign clearly enough: ruthlessness in the dynastic struggle, effective consolidation, and skilful exploitation of his father's holy reputation. He is remembered as a successful Erik partisan who entrenched his family's claim rather than as a vividly individual character.

contentSections.title: As king of Sweden
paragraphs: Knut Eriksson took power after dynastic conflict and ruled for a comparatively long period. His reign helped stabilize the Erik line.
As King of Sweden, Knut Eriksson had to turn dynastic claim into workable authority through alliances, military pressure, church support, and acceptance by regional elites.

contentSections.title: Death
paragraphs: Died in 1195 or 1196 after a long reign; his sons later renewed the succession struggle with the Sverker line.

contentSections.title: Legacy
paragraphs: He is remembered as a stabilizing ruler in Sweden’s twelfth-century dynastic rivalry.
Later saga, saintly, or national traditions often amplified Knut Eriksson's reputation, so the article separates near-contemporary evidence from later memory where possible.
